title: Virat Kohli Meets Maharashtra Deputy CM Eknath Shinde in London
excerpt: The goodwill meeting during Shinde's UK visit covered sports, infrastructure, and state welfare schemes; the Deputy CM felicitated Kohli with a shawl and bouquet.
body:
• Virat Kohli met Maharashtra Deputy Chief Minister Eknath Shinde in London on Friday during Shinde's UK visit, calling it a goodwill meeting.
  • The two discussed sports, infrastructure, and Maharashtra government welfare schemes; Shinde felicitated Kohli with a shawl and bouquet.
  • Shinde told ANI that Kohli, who lives in London, "himself remarked that the development Maharashtra has seen in recent years is unprecedented."
  • The meeting follows Shinde's engagements at the House of Lords and events aimed at deepening Maharashtra-U.K. economic ties.

Indian batting icon Virat Kohli met Maharashtra Deputy Chief Minister Eknath Shinde in London on Friday, with the two discussing sports, infrastructure, and various government schemes initiated by the state government during what Shinde described as a courtesy meeting.

Shinde felicitated the former India captain with a shawl and bouquet as the two posed for cameras, according to ANI footage shared on social media. The deputy chief minister, dressed formally, and Kohli, in a casual full-sleeve T-shirt, were later seen in conversation after the photographs.

Speaking to ANI after the meeting, Shinde described Kohli as "down-to-earth" and said the cricketer had sought him out on learning he was in the city.

"Virat Kohli lives in London, and when he learned that I am here, he met me for a goodwill visit. I was delighted that such a big Indian cricketer, the one with the most centuries, is so down-to-earth."

— Eknath Shinde, Maharashtra Deputy Chief Minister

Shinde's packed London itinerary

The Kohli meeting came during a London visit in which Shinde has been engaging with investors and diaspora stakeholders. At the House of Lords, Shinde defended Maharashtra's Ladki Bahin scheme as "not charity" but "a measure of women's empowerment," according to the Deccan Herald. He also announced that the next global Marathi literary meet will be held in London, paid homage to Babasaheb Ambedkar at his London residence — calling the site a "holy spot" — and made the case for deeper Maharashtra-U.K. economic ties, according to The Hindu, The Tribune, and ThePrint.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=oe3k4_7PFy8

On the welfare and infrastructure front, Shinde told ANI he walked Kohli through the state's future plans and projects currently underway, including the "Third Mumbai" development near the airport, the Atal Setu, the Balasaheb Thackeray Samruddhi Mahamarg, the coastal road, and metro expansion, along with initiatives in schools and healthcare.

Diaspora angle

The meeting plays directly to the UK's large Marathi and Indian diaspora, for whom Kohli remains the most recognizable Indian sports figure and Shinde's announcements — a global Marathi literary meet in London, the Ambedkar homage — carry cultural weight. Kohli, who divides his time between India and London, has become a recurring bridge between Indian political outreach and the diaspora: his presence turns a policy briefing into an event the community actually watches.

What's next

Kohli returns to the field next in India's three-match ODI series against the West Indies at home, after scoring 144 runs at an average of 48.00 with two fifties in the recent ODI series against England. Shinde's London outreach continues the Maharashtra government's pitch to UK investors — and the visuals with Kohli give the state a celebrity-sized spotlight back home.
